previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of CAD s/p CABG, COPD, chronic diastolic heart failure, hypothyroidism, and alcohol abuse was admitted after his physical therapist noted bradycardia with a heart rate in the 40s. He reported chronic lightheadedness but denied new symptoms such as chest pain, syncope, or worsening dyspnea. Evaluation included telemetry, EKG showing sinus bradycardia, normal cardiac enzymes, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Thyroid function was normal, and no medication adjustments were made. His bradycardia was deemed asymptomatic and not requiring intervention. He remained stable, continued on his outpatient medications including acamprosate and thiamine, and was discharged home with services and follow-up instructions for dizziness and cardiac care.
